solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 29ac.
Foul Boris's ultimate title: "New TV Celeb"

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of Boris's name is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Boris's
a tag is a label or title
N is the standard abbreviation for new
Ant McPartlin, of the presenting duo Ant and Dec, is a British TV celebrity

explanation.surface: A scornful verdict on Boris Johnson's latest billing as a fresh television personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is stale and foul-smelling because it does not flow.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Doesn't hold back, tries pathetically to break record

indicators.note: done pathetically means done badly, so the word tries is botched into a new order
breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go into the record

blocks.note: an LP is a long-playing record
the word tries rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone holding nothing back makes a feeble attempt to set a new record.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting without restraint, giving full vent to energy or feeling.

clue.text: Downfall after political leader, embraced by Nazis, turns

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter of political is taken
after places the downfall immediately behind the political leader in the line
something embraced is held in the arms of another, so the Nazis wrap around the rest

blocks.note: the first half of SS, Hitler's Nazi paramilitary
the opening letter of political
rain is a downfall from the sky
the second half of SS

explanation.surface: A political leader caught by Nazis meets his downfall in a sudden reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The SS were the Nazi paramilitary, so 'Nazis' gives SS, which wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain a joint is to wrench or twist it, as when an ankle turns awkwardly.

clue.text: Prominent row in Commons about not taking Brexit lead (tearing into foreigners)

indicators.note: the lead is what goes first, so only the opening letter of Brexit counts
about here means turned around, so the letters are jumbled
tearing into something means bursting inside it, so the jumble sits within the foreigners

blocks.note: the start of FRENCH, people from abroad
taken as written
the opening letter of Brexit
the rest of FRENCH

explanation.surface: A noisy Commons row over Brexit, with someone laying into foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The French stand in for foreigners; the jumble of NOT plus B goes inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The front benches in the House of Commons are the prominent seats occupied by ministers and their opposition counterparts.

clue.text: Load of women rowers

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A boatload of female rowers out on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy burden or something carried, as in a load on the shoulders.

clue.text: Pop star: flash, fishy thing

blocks.note: Sting is the singer, formerly of The Police
a ray is a flash or beam of light

explanation.surface: A gossipy remark that a flashy pop star seems somehow suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests something suspicious, but here it is literal: the answer is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat sea creature with a venomous tail barb is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Substance? Ex-leader's lost half

indicators.note: losing half means one of the two halves of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Pol Pot was the former leader of Cambodia's Khmer Rouge

explanation.surface: A question about whether a former leader, having lost half his support, has any substance left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substance' sounds like weight or depth, but it is a drug; Pol Pot drops his first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, an illicit substance in the sense of a drug.

clue.text: Deputation from English politician that hurt Brenda – intended, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means what follows is to be heard spoken rather than read

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an MP is a Member of Parliament
ow is the cry of someone who has just been hurt
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
meant is a word for intended

explanation.surface: An English MP deliberately caused the Queen pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputation is the act of delegating authority to someone, which is the sense of granting power.

clue.text: Wire-tapped party oddball

indicators.note: tapped is slang for crazy, so the word wire goes mad and changes order

blocks.note: wire rearranged
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A bugged party where someone odd was listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wire-tapped' reads as bugged, but the hyphen hides a crazy-sounding anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is a slang term for a strange or eccentric person.

clue.text: see 12ac.
(& 20dn./11ac.) "Diffusing continental gigolo slur": Obama's big frustration?

indicators.note: diffusing means spreading out and scattering, so the quoted words are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of the three quoted words

explanation.surface: A headline about defusing an insult aimed at a European lothario, oddly linked to Barack Obama.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Obama repeatedly failed to pass tighter firearms laws through Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Obama tried and failed several times to get firearms restrictions through Congress, calling it one of his greatest frustrations.

clue.text: Tin Tin's suggestive high kicks, etc.

blocks.note: a tin is a can
a tin again

explanation.surface: Tintin, the boy reporter of the comic books, doing racy high kicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin Tin' recalls Hergé's comic hero Tintin, but it is simply tin twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively French dance, famed in Parisian music halls, features high kicks and skirt-lifting thought risqué.

clue.text: Nick involved in broadcast of a Corbyn clone

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it, so nick goes into the middle
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of a and Corbyn rearranged
to nick, in British slang, is to arrest, as is to cop

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick appears on air as Jeremy Corbyn's double.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a name, but cop and nick both mean arrest in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon copy is an exact duplicate, so figuratively a person who closely resembles another.

clue.text: Parliamentarian getting sack over poor rate?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for sack is read backwards
poor means in bad shape, so the letters of rate are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed
the letters of rate rearranged

explanation.surface: An MP is fired over a poor approval rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the sack' suggests dismissal, but sack here means bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentarian is someone who argues motions in a legislative chamber, so one who debates.

clue.text: Piece about repulsive Tyson?

indicators.note: something repulsive drives things back, so the short word is turned backwards

blocks.note: a bit is a piece
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the boxer Mike Tyson's repugnant behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Mike Tyson bit off part of Evander Holyfield's ear in a 1997 fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyson famously sank his teeth into an opponent's ear during a title fight, earning him that label.

clue.text: Slip on this after having wet yourself?

definitions.text: Slip on this after having wet yourself?

blocks.clueFragment: Slip on this after having wet yourself?
blocks.note: surface reading: an embarrassing accident and a skid on the puddle

blocks.clueFragment: Slip on this after having wet yourself?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the garment you put on after soaking in a tub

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip on' means put on, as clothing, and 'wet yourself' means getting soaked while washing.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose towelling gown is worn after bathing to dry off and keep warm.

clue.text: (& 27dn.) Shag extremely playfully, reckless – a minor irritation

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends of playfully

blocks.note: shag is a thick pile on cloth or carpet, and so is nap
the first and last letters of playfully
rash means reckless

explanation.surface: A playful, reckless sexual encounter dismissed as a small annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag is rude British slang, but here it means a carpet pile; the minor is a baby, and a nappy is a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaper rash is a skin inflammation affecting babies, a sore that troubles infants, who are minors.

clue.text: Follow-on from preliminary stage: stuffing knocked out of Trump – ah, woes afresh!

indicators.note: knocking the stuffing out empties the inside, leaving just the outer letters of Trump
afresh means anew, so the letters are set out again in a new order

blocks.note: Trump with its middle removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Donald Trump is humbled at last, and his troubles begin all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: The second phase of a project is what follows on once the initial stage is complete.

clue.text: Knocked back about a barrel "to get accustomed"

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for knocked back goes round the barrel

blocks.note: to knock back food or drink is to consume it
a tun is a large beer or wine cask

explanation.surface: Someone downs a whole barrel just to get used to the stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests rebuffed, but it means swallowed; the 'a' before barrel is just the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune oneself is to adjust or become used to something, bringing oneself into harmony with it.

clue.text: see 12ac.
Chuck: clod, openly gay

blocks.note: a clod is a lump of earth or turf
out means openly gay

explanation.surface: A lump of earth and a dull name tag, Chuck the clod, revealed as openly gay.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck reads as a man's name; it is the verb for throwing someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: To turf someone out is British informal for ejecting them, just as to chuck someone means to throw them out.

clue.text: Right and Left hold record each for withdrawal

indicators.note: to hold is to grip around, so the outer pair encloses the others

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
an EP is an extended-play record
ea is the abbreviation for each
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Politicians of Right and Left each claim a record of retreating on policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Repealing a law means revoking it, the formal withdrawal of legislation.

clue.text: Randy's working ex-PM (not hard)

indicators.note: not hard says the letter standing for hard must be taken away

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: Randy, at work, is a former Prime Minister who isn't up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard, dropped from Heath's end.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal in its fertile period is sexually receptive, and figuratively a person feeling lustful is likewise.

clue.text: Panic? Brenda's over it

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... of agitation, as in getting into a ...
second meaning: the Queen, nicknamed Brenda by Private Eye, is head of the nation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is panic, and is told the Queen has got past it.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen 'Brenda'; she is head of state, so she is over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flustered condition of mind and a nation or polity headed by a sovereign.

clue.text: see 3dn.
Temperature taken after energy-charged, wild erotic fun – not for real

indicators.note: charged means loaded with something added, so energy is put in among the letters before they are shuffled
wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
taken after puts the temperature at the end of everything else

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
the two words letter for letter
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Things heat up during some wild, energetic erotic fun that turns out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit goods are forged imitations, fakes passed off as genuine.

clue.text: see 17ac.
Swearing hapless bum is buggered without love

indicators.note: buggered is British slang for broken, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
without here means outside, so the jumble goes round love

blocks.note: the letters of both words rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A luckless loafer, ruined and unloved, cursing his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a string of oaths, fitting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasphemous speech is profane, irreverent cursing, which is one sense of swearing.

clue.text: (& 1dn.) Hardly Thatcher's type (though having charm) – "holiday-wrecker"

blocks.note: Margaret Thatcher scornfully called the moderate Tories in her cabinet 'wets'; she was no such thing
a charm is a magic spell

explanation.surface: A jibe at Thatcher's cabinet moderates, dismissed as soft and charming types who ruin everyone's fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wets' were the moderate Conservatives Thatcher distrusted; the bracketed 'though having charm' supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of rainy days is exactly what ruins a seaside break or camping trip.
